title: Endurance Car Warranty Exposed: What They Don’t Tell You | PissedConsumer
summary: A review of Endurance customer complaints: high prices relative to repairs, denied claims over pre-existing conditions and missing records, and slow approvals despite fast-sounding marketing.

assertions.quote: the company argues the damage must have existed before you signed up, even if your mechanic says otherwise

verdicts.note: A frequently reported denial reason, though providers also sometimes legitimately identify real pre-existing damage.

assertions.quote: Miss a single oil change receipt, that alone can be grounds to stall or deny a claim

verdicts.note: A frequently reported denial tactic, though maintenance requirements can also be legitimate when directly relevant to the failed part.
Same FTC passage: missing maintenance records can get a claim denied, but the guide doesn't address whether the missing record is unrelated to the actual failure.

assertions.quote: 48 business hours just for reconsideration, which isn't the same as getting back on the road quickly

verdicts.note: Documented discrepancy between marketed turnaround and contract definitions.

assertions.quote: Shops cannot even move forward on a repair without insurance's pre-authorization

verdicts.note: A standard contractual requirement reported to extend repair timelines.

assertions.quote: seals and gaskets aren't really covered under Insurance's Secure Plus or Superior plans
